newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-RODMAN TO BE REINSTATED AFTER ALL-STAR BREAK.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-RODMAN TO BE REINSTATED AFTER ALL-STAR BREAK.

text.p: Dennis Rodman's suspension will end following the NBA's All-Star break and the controversial Bulls forward will be reinstated for Chicago's February 11 game against Charlotte, commissioner David Stern said Tuesday.
Rodman had been fined and suspended without pay for kicking a cameraman during a game against the Minnesota Timberwolves on January 15.
"I am satisfied that Dennis recognises that his conduct in the Minnesota game was unacceptable," Stern said in a statement.

"Dennis told me that while he does not plan to change the way he plays the game, he will conform his conduct on the playing court to acceptable standards, and he knows that any further incidents of this nature may end his career in the NBA."
Stern met with Rodman in New York last Friday.
Rodman, who has already missed nine games, will miss a total of 11 games in the second-longest suspension ever served in the NBA.
The defending champion Bulls, however, have not missed a beat, winning eight of those games heading into Tuesday night's contest at Portland.

Besides the loss of salary, Rodman was also fined $25,000 for his actions and directed to undergo psychiatric counselling by the league. Rodman, 35, reportedly agreed to a $200,000 out-of-court settlement with the cameraman.
The length of Rodman's suspension is second only to the 26-game ban given to Kermit Washington of the Los Angeles Lakers for punching Rudy Tomjanovich of Houston in 1977.

It is the second suspension of the season for Rodman, who served a two-game, team-imposed suspension earlier this season for a profanity-laced tirade on the referees in December. That suspension cost him $219,512, or 2/82nd of his 1996-97 salary of $9 million.

The five-time rebounding champion with the multi-coloured hair and multiple tattoos has had numerous run-ins with officials, including the head-butting of a referee last March at New Jersey that earned him a six-game suspension.
Rodman came back from that suspension to help Chicago to a record 72-10 mark and its fourth championship in six years.
